expected: A tax page opened after a session of live trading should default to the year the ledger actually has activity in (or the current calendar year), not to a year that happens to have none. The copy shown for the wrong default is itself accurate and well-written -- this is not the messaging defect the last two Tax-page findings were (activity-year-contradicts-count, zero-disposals-boilerplate) -- it is the selection that lands on the wrong year in the first place, which undermines that earlier fix by showing its honest-but-irrelevant output first.
observed: After session 1's two fills (SPY, TLT bought 2026-07-20; account funded 2026-07-17), I opened /tax. document.querySelector('select').value read '2025' on load -- not '2026'. The panel read: 'No 2025 activity at all. The ledger holds 3 transactions, none of them dated in this tax year -- pick another year above.' Manually setting the select to 2026 (native setter + change event) immediately produced the correct read: 'Nothing was disposed of in 2026. The ledger holds 3 transactions dated in this tax year -- see Activity -- but no lot was sold, so there is no gain or loss to report and no Form 8949 to file for it.' The <select>'s option list is 2026, 2025, 2024... in that order -- 2026 is literally the first option in the DOM -- yet the control opens on the second one.
repro: Trade so the ledger has 2026-dated transactions only (this run's sandbox: funded 2026-07-17, bought SPY+TLT 2026-07-20)
Observe the placeholder: 'No 2025 activity at all... pick another year above'
Set the select to '2026' via the native HTMLSelectElement value setter + a dispatched 'change' event
Observe the correct message: 'Nothing was disposed of in 2026... no gain or loss to report'
suggested_fix: Default the selector to the most recent year that has ledger activity (or the current calendar year), rather than a fixed offset from today.
title: Tax page's year selector defaults to a year with no activity instead of the ledger's actual year

verification.note: `useState(currentYear - 1)` opens the page on 2025 against a ledger holding only 2026 rows. Defensible in January when filing last year's return, wrong the rest of the year. Filed independently by all three runs; every one of them read the empty year as a failed import, which is the failure mode that makes it major rather than cosmetic.

why_it_matters: Tax review is the last step of my session process, and it is where I'd notice the discrepancy between what I traded and what's shown. On first look this page tells a trader who just made three transactions that the ledger has 'no activity at all' for the selected year. That reads as 'the app isn't tracking my tax exposure,' not 'you're on the wrong year' -- there is no visual cue that 2025 was chosen for me rather than by me. A user who trusts the first screen and doesn't think to check the dropdown walks away believing tax tracking is broken.

expected: The application's derived settled/unsettled split should agree with the paper broker's own settlement accounting to the cent, since both are reading the same ledger. A sale's regulatory fee (recorded as its own FEE row per this ledger's design) belongs with the unsettled proceeds it was deducted from, not against the previously-settled balance -- the fee only exists because of a trade that has not settled yet.
observed: I sold 10 TLT this session: gross proceeds $837.00, a $0.02 fee, net cash_delta $836.98 (all three numbers are in the fill record and the paper broker's own book_after.settled_cash, which read exactly '1750.68' after the fill). The very next order I placed was rejected with 'reason: $2231.34 exceeds $1750.68 of settled cash' -- so the broker's own enforcement engine used $1,750.68 as spendable settled cash, correctly netting the $0.02 fee out of the settled side (settled cash was unaffected by an unsettled trade's fee) and leaving $836.98 as the unsettled proceeds. But the application's own /api/portfolio, ingested from the very same session's fills, reports settled_cash '1750.66' and cash_by_account[0] = {settled: '1750.66', unsettled: '837.00', balance: '2587.66'}. The total ($2,587.66) matches the broker exactly. The split does not: settled is $0.02 low, unsettled is $0.02 high -- the two errors cancel in the total but land on the wrong side of the settled/unsettled line individually.
repro: From a book with only settled cash, sell a position so the sale carries a fee row (this run: SELL TLT 10 in session 2, fee $0.02, net proceeds $836.98)
Read the fill record / paper-broker book_after.settled_cash -- it nets the fee out of the unsettled side (here: $1,750.68 settled, implying $836.98 unsettled)
Fetch GET /api/portfolio (or read the Portfolio page's CASH tile / Cash by Account table) for the same session
Compare: application reports settled '1750.66' (two cents lower) and unsettled '837.00' (two cents higher, the un-netted gross proceeds)
suggested_fix: When deriving the unsettled bucket for a still-unsettled sale, net that sale's own FEE row(s) out of the unsettled proceeds rather than out of the running settled balance.
title: Settled/unsettled cash split misattributes a sale's fee to settled cash instead of the unsettled proceeds it came from

verification.note: The `t.amount > 0` filter admits a pending sale's gross proceeds to `unsettled` but excludes the separate negative FEE row, which is nevertheless in `balance`. So `settled = balance - unsettled` is short by exactly the fee and `unsettled` is high by it. Reproduced twice with the arithmetic scaling: $0.02 on TLT, $0.06 on QQQ. The total is right and the partition is wrong, which matters because this file documents `settled` as answering 'what can I deploy'. Magnitude here is amplified by the harness writing fees as their own rows; real Robinhood exports net them into the sell.

why_it_matters: I size positions against 'settled cash' because that is the number the broker actually enforces -- and it is the number I'd read off this page to decide what I can spend today. It disagreed with the broker's own enforcement by $0.02 in this session; on an account with more trading and more fee rows the same misattribution compounds every session and the two ledgers (what the broker will actually let me spend, and what the portfolio page tells me I can spend) drift apart. A two-cent gap I catch by accident is a two-cent gap I won't catch when it's buried in a real multi-fee week.
